offers.label: Hardware-only trackball control-station kit
offers.description: We manufacture and sell furniture + certified third-party control hardware only. Customer brings their own legally-owned TV, PC, and game software/emulation or a legitimate donor system they source and integrate themselves. This is the only offer with no unresolved IP/royalty cost line, because no game software or licensed content is distributed — but that is NOT the same as 'legally clean,' pre-certified, or launch-ready: ordinary consumer-goods obligations (electrical/EMC compliance for the assembled unit, CPSC consumer-product rules to the extent they apply, bound general/product liability insurance, business registration) remain unresolved and gated (see killCriteria K3, goNoGo).
offers.legalModel: Hardware-only consumer product: no game software or licensed game content is included, so this model carries no game-distribution royalty line. That does not eliminate intellectual-property, component-license, consumer-protection or product-safety obligations. Verify the actual components' certifications and determine applicable electrical/EMC and CPSC requirements with qualified counsel/a compliance lab for the released assembly; a CPSC General Certificate of Conformity is required only where an applicable rule requires it. A listed power supply does not certify the finished product.

offers.label: Donor-system integration service
offers.description: Customer already owns or independently sources a legitimate donor arcade system (e.g. a real Silver Strike Nighthawk kit, a legacy Eagle-era Big Buck PCB set, or a 2015 Raw Thrills Jurassic Park Arcade electronics/I-O/dongle assembly). We build/rebuild the furniture shell around their hardware and bench-test it. We do not supply, copy, or modify any game software, ROM, BIOS, or security/identity device, and we do not promise or warrant the legality, completeness, or functionality of the customer's donor system beyond 'demonstrably worked immediately before and after our integration work.'
offers.legalModel: Bespoke labor + materials service. Adds bailment exposure (temporary custody of the customer's possibly irreplaceable hardware) requiring its own liability terms, a signed customer waiver/scope-of-work, and a higher damage reserve than the hardware-only product warranty.

offers.label: Fully licensed turnkey cabinet (all-inclusive, pre-loaded game)
offers.description: A complete cabinet including display, PC, and a specific licensed game, ready to play out of the box. This is the product Mike's original four-game vision implies, but it cannot be priced, built, or sold without a signed license/royalty agreement with the applicable rights holder (Incredible Technologies for Golden Tee/Silver Strike IP; Raw Thrills/Play Mechanix for Big Buck Hunter/Jurassic Park Arcade IP). No such agreement exists. The companies named here are each title's arcade-cabinet licensor of record, not a confirmed-complete rights chain — Jurassic Park Arcade in particular sits on top of the separately-held Jurassic Park film property, and no confirmation was found that Raw Thrills/Play Mechanix alone can grant all rights needed for a new licensed home SKU. This offer is modeled to show its cost structure and the explicit blocking gap — not because it is ready to sell, and not as a claim that the named companies are the only or complete rights-holder chain.
offers.legalModel: BLOCKED. Requires a negotiated IP license (and likely hardware/software approval) from the rights holder before any price, deposit, or unit can be offered. No public rate card was found for this class of agreement at small-manufacturer scale; treat the license/royalty line as an unresolved, non-zero unknown, not an assumption. For Jurassic Park Arcade specifically, 'the rights holder' may be more than one party (arcade publisher plus film-property owner); no complete rights-holder chain has been identified or confirmed.

Three unrelated paid pilots with positive stressed contribution, followed by successful fulfillment/support acceptance; then apply K1's distinct 10-unit funding gate
Revalidate demand, landed quotes and capacity before 50/100-unit commitments; pilot orders are not an annual-volume forecast

killCriteria.rule: Do not commit batch_10 NRE/tooling spend (~$1,300-2,900) until at least 6 of 10 units have a collected 50% deposit, OR the owner explicitly accepts the full launch-liquidity requirement shown in economics.csv's launchLiquidityRequiredUsd for batch_10 (see production-plan.md section 6) — that figure is a floor cash requirement, not a risk-free number, even before any deposits are counted.

At $1,799, batch_10 has negative marginal contribution (-0.5%) at baseline, before tooling. There is no universal safe price floor: recompute the selected batch using its landed quotes, paid labor, CAC and stress case; then recover tooling and operating overhead separately.

Before a commercial pilot or batch, bind suitable liability coverage, document which safety/electrical/EMC rules apply to the actual released product, and complete their required testing and certification with qualified advice. A CPSC General Certificate of Conformity is required only if an applicable rule requires it; listed components do not certify the assembly.

Do not accept a customer's donor hardware into the shop without a signed bailment/liability waiver, and never represent or imply that integration confers any software license or legality to the customer's donor system.

Do not quote a price or collect any deposit for the licensed_turnkey offer until a signed license/royalty agreement exists with the applicable rights holder establishing an actual per-unit license cost. Do not substitute $0 or an invented placeholder.

Re-gate before committing to batch_50/batch_100: if real material quotes (including the inbound-freight/procurement-tax allowance) vary more than 15% from the ~$828 material baseline, or a real CNC nesting quote implies more sheets than the conservative 55%-utilization placeholder, treat as a hard stop requiring re-pricing, not a rounding error.

If a real marketing test shows CAC above ~$450/order (the upper end tested), the paid-acquisition channel for the hardware-only consumer SKU should be killed in favor of the lower-CAC donor-integration/referral path, or the hardware-only commercial path should be shelved entirely.

At +30% direct-cost stress (a realistic landed-cost miss given zero vendor quotes obtained), batch_10's MARGINAL contribution margin goes negative at the $2,199 test price, not just its batch-fully-loaded margin (see economics.csv) — the batch would lose money on every unit sold, before tooling is even considered. Do not treat batch_10 baseline numbers as a cushion against normal quoting variance; re-run the model against real quotes before committing cash.

The donor-integration service's own standalone tooling ($900, see nreTotalUsd) exceeds what a SINGLE job's marginal contribution margin can cover at any tested stress level — batchFullyLoadedMarginUsd is negative for donor_integration_job at 0%, +15%, and +30% stress alike. Do not describe a first donor-integration job as self-funding, zero-risk, or the strongest number in this analysis; it needs the same pre-validated-volume or owner-funded-tooling reasoning as batch_10 before being offered commercially (see goNoGo.conditionsForOfferingDonorIntegrationCommercially).

goNoGo.recommendation: PERSONAL PROTOTYPE FIRST. Do not release a commercial batch or accept customer hardware before the demand, compliance, funding and support gates below. A hardware-only kit priced near a complete factory Fore! preorder needs a validated differentiator beyond price; preorder acceptance is not proof of shipment. See narrative.json for the exact competing configurations and availability limits.
conditionsForCommercialLaunchOfHardwareO: Prototype built and passes PLAN.md's own build-acceptance gates (trackball/button/fit/safety tests)

Three unrelated paid pilot orders at a price with positive stressed contribution, followed by successful fulfillment and support acceptance. Then apply K1's separately funded or deposit-backed 10-unit batch gate; three pilots are not proof of demand for 50 units.
Liability/product insurance bound; applicable product-safety, electrical/EMC and certification requirements established and completed for the released design, with qualified counsel/lab review

A differentiation story beyond price that a complete factory cabinet cannot offer — e.g. multi-game flexibility for a customer's own legal ROM/donor library, custom furniture integration, or the specific classic (non-reboot) Silver Strike/legacy Big Buck gap — validated with at least a few real prospective buyers, not asserted
conditionsForOfferingDonorIntegrationCom: Liability insurance covering custody of third-party property bound
At least one real inquiry from someone who already owns or has a credible path to a legitimate donor system

A funding plan for the $900 standalone furniture-shell tooling investment (owner-funded up front, or pre-validated volume sufficient to amortize it) — do not rely on a single job's deposit to cover it (see killCriteria K9)
